title: At the table
subtitle: Serving and pairing Dolcetto
objectives: Know how long to keep it

steps.title: Everyday food
steps.body: Dolcetto suits everyday Piedmontese food: salumi, vitello tonnato, agnolotti pasta, pizza, roast chicken and mild cheeses. Its soft acidity and moderate tannin make it easy with many dishes. Its bitter finish works well with fatty charcuterie.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve at 14 to 16 degrees, slightly cooler than big reds. Most Dolcetto is best within two to three years of the vintage, when fruit is fresh. Dogliani Superiore can age five to eight years. It's usually made in steel, without much oak.

steps.explanation: Sweet desserts make dry reds taste sour.

steps.title: A mealtime wine
steps.body: In Piedmont, Dolcetto is often the wine on the table at lunch, while Barolo and Barbaresco wait for special occasions or long ageing. It's honest and fruity rather than complex, and that's its charm.

steps.prompt: Most Dolcetto is best drunk within two to three years.
steps.explanation: Yes. Its charm is fresh, dark fruit.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Dolcetto suits salumi, pasta and pizza
Serve at 14 to 16 degrees, within two to three years
